deep.reconstruction:
Context. This is the second sheet of a laboratory record dated 12 March 1836 at the Göttingen observatory, 7.4 °C. It belongs to the Gauss–Weber induction experiments. A magnetometer needle swings inside a multiplier coil. With the circuit open ('Kette offen') the swing dies away slowly. With the circuit closed ('Kette geschlossen') induced currents damp it much more strongly. The page continues the numbered sequence of turning-point observations begun on the previous page.

Columns. The first column is the number n of the swing. The second gives the clock time, entered only at the first swing of each group. Next comes a scale value: probably the computed rest position, which drifts slowly from 989 to 977 over the session. The fourth column is the amplitude A_n in scale units. The last column is log10 A_n, written to 5 decimals.

Spot checks of the logarithms (mine):
- log10 723.55 = 2.85947
- log10 657.8 = 2.81809
- log10 607.2 = 2.78333

Step 1: five-swing means. For each group of five consecutive swings Gauss takes the arithmetic mean of the logs. This gives the log-amplitude at the middle swing, written in units of 1e-5 with one extra digit:
- swings 51–55: (2.85947+2.85715+2.85503+2.85266+2.85009)/5 = 2.854880, written 2.85488.0;
- swings 69–73: mean = 2.813368, written 2.81336.8;
- swings 77–81: mean = 2.767750, written 2.76775.0;
- swings 94–98: mean = 2.635294, written 2.63529.4.
Averaging logarithms is equivalent to fitting ln A_n = a − λn by least squares over symmetric equally spaced points; the middle swing is the centroid.

Step 2: logarithmic decrement per swing ('D.L.'), in units of 1e-5 of the common log.
- Circuit open, middle swings 53 and 71, 18 swings apart: (2.854880 − 2.813368)/18 = 0.0023062, written D.L. 230.62.
- Circuit closed, middle swings 79 and 96, 17 swings apart: (2.767750 − 2.635294)/17 = 0.0077915, written D.L. 779.15.

Step 3: the margin numbers 11½, 36½, 62, 87½, 112½ are the start of the recapitulation completed on the next page. They are the midpoints of the swing pairs used for each decrement:
- (3+20)/2 = 11½ and (28+45)/2 = 36½, from the previous page;
- (53+71)/2 = 62 and (79+96)/2 = 87½, from this page;
- (104+121)/2 = 112½, from the next page.
The purpose of the recapitulation is to interpolate the open-circuit decrement at the epochs of the closed-circuit decrements, and conversely. The difference closed − open is the damping due to the induced current alone, about 538 units (mean 538.42 on the next page). The entries 102–123 in the right margin are the beginning of the next sheet's data, cut off by the image edge.

Period (implicit, mine). The timings give the period:
- swings 51→69: 762.65 s over 18 swings = 42.37 s;
- swings 77→94: 720.1 s over 17 swings = 42.36 s.
This agrees with the previous page (720.15 s / 17 = 42.36 s), so the timing is internally consistent.
errors: In swings 94–98 the amplitude column repeats the rest-position column (978.15, 978.48, 978.60, 978.65, 978.55) instead of the amplitudes. The logarithms are correct for amplitudes of about 447.65, 439.4, 431.8, 424.3 and 416.5. This is a copying slip that does not affect the results (10^2.65099 ≈ 447.6, not 978.15).
All four five-swing means and both decrements (230.62, 779.15) check exactly to the digits written. The logarithms checked (723.55, 657.8, 607.2) are correct to 5 decimals.

Not on this page: the next page's interpolated open-circuit values 224.29 and 262.03 are not simple averages of neighbouring decrements (224.355 and 261.72). They may use time-weighted interpolation or a different scheme; this cannot be verified from this page alone.

results.what: Reduction of oscillation amplitudes by averaging log-amplitudes over groups of five swings and dividing the difference of group means by the swing interval, giving the logarithmic decrement per swing.
results.modern_name: Logarithmic decrement of a damped oscillator, estimated by least-squares/averaging of ln-amplitudes
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss and Weber (Göttingen Magnetic Union, 1830s); the damping concept was developed by Weber

results.what: Separation of the electromagnetic induction damping (closed minus open circuit decrement, about 538 units of 1e-5 log10) by interpolating the open-circuit decrement in time.
results.modern_name: Eddy/induction-current damping of a galvanometer/magnetometer (electromagnetic damping)
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss and W. Weber (1830s); Weber's later published damping theory

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine experimental data reduction from the well-documented Gauss–Weber induction and magnetometer damping work of 1836. The logarithmic decrement method is known to be theirs. Nothing non-standard appears.

checkable.asserts: log10 of amplitude 607.2 is 2.78333 (confirms the reading 607.2)
true amplitudes for swings 94–98 are about 447.6, 439.4, 431.8, 424.3, 416.5, not 978.x
rough elapsed-time check (simplified); the properly converted interval 34'0.9" − 21'18.25" = 762.65 s gives a period of 762.65/18 ≈ 42.37 s

transcription_corrections: 'D.L. 23062[?]' should read 'D.L. 230.62', confirmed by the computation and by the recapitulation on the next page.
The amplitude for swing 77 is 607.2, consistent with its log 2.78333.
In swings 94–98 the duplicated numbers are genuinely on the manuscript (Gauss's slip), not a transcription error.
The right-margin numbers 11½ … 112½ are the swing-midpoint epochs of the recapitulation (decrement epochs), not stray entries. Numbers 102–123 belong to the next sheet's data columns.
